Side AB is the base, AD is the long slanted side from D to A, and BC and CD form an inward notch; therefore it can be regarded as the large triangle ABD with the small triangle BCD removed. Reasoning: Connect BD. It is known that ∠BCD is a right angle, BC=4, CD=3, so triangle BCD is a 3-4-5 right triangle, and BD=5. Its area is (1/2)×4×3=6. Also AB=12, AD=13, BD=5, so the three sides of triangle ABD are 5, 12, 13, making it a right triangle, with area (1/2)×5×12=30. The quadrilateral ABCD in the figure is the large triangle ABD minus the inwardly concave small triangle BCD, so its area is 30-6=24.
